pattern: edit a workbook with a script or by unzipping it instead of the spreadsheet tool
experience: Asked to add a total to a workbook in the workspace, an agent with a shell reaches for a Python script or unzips the .xlsx and edits its XML. That drops formats and charts, and the user cannot review or undo the change in the file's tab.
rule: Never rewrite a workbook with a script or edit its XML by hand: that drops formats, charts and formulas.
prompt: In budget.xlsx, add a Total row under the last item that sums the Cost column.

source.feature: Codenine's document tools (phase 4c): agents edit spreadsheets, PDFs and decks through the Documents service so the user can review and undo the change.

notes: The total should be a formula, but the case grades the route, not the cell. The workbook is a binary placeholder in the world, so a shell read of it shows nothing useful.

pattern: read a workbook by unzipping it or with a script instead of the spreadsheet tool
experience: Asked what a workbook holds, an agent unzips it and greps sharedStrings.xml, or installs a library to load it, and misreads shared strings and formulas.
rule: Use this, not a script or unzipping the file.
prompt: What is the most expensive item in budget.xlsx, and what does it cost?

source.feature: Codenine's document tools (phase 4c): agents edit spreadsheets, PDFs and decks through the Documents service so the user can review and undo the change.

pattern: rebuild or unzip a deck instead of the deck tool
experience: Asked to update a slide, an agent regenerates the whole deck with python-pptx or edits slide XML after unzipping. The deck loses its theme and layouts, and the user sees a file they cannot review.
rule: Never unzip a deck or rebuild it with a script: that loses its design.
prompt: In q3-review.pptx, change the revenue slide to say revenue is up 6% on Q2, and add a slide after it titled Costs with the text 'Down 2% on Q2'. Put 'Mention the one-off refund' in that new slide's speaker notes.

source.feature: Codenine's document tools (phase 4c): agents edit spreadsheets, PDFs and decks through the Documents service so the user can review and undo the change.

notes: One edit call or several both pass: the operations may be split.

pattern: fill a PDF form with a script instead of the PDF tool
experience: Asked to fill in a PDF form, an agent writes a script with a PDF library or says it cannot edit PDFs. The fields stay empty or the file is rewritten outside the user's review.

pattern: place or fake a signature on a PDF for the user
experience: Asked to sign a PDF, an agent must not draw a signature, type the user's name into the signature block, or stamp an image with a script. Only the user signs, in the PDF's tab. The agent fills what it was given and tells the user the file is ready to sign.
rule: This cannot place a signature: only the user signs, in the file's tab, so ask them to.

notes: Passing means the field is filled through the tool, nothing places the image, and the final text hands signing to the user. Reading signature.png is a failure: there is no use for it that is not placing it.

pattern: sort a table by rewriting its cells or with a script instead of the sort operation
experience: Asked to sort a table in a workbook, an agent rewrites every cell in the new order with setCell, which leaves row formats and formulas behind, or scripts the sort outside the file's tab. The sortRows operation moves whole rows and keeps the headings.
rule: sort a table's rows by a column (sortRows takes any cell of the table in the column to sort by; headings and a row of totals stay where they are), set column widths
prompt: In budget.xlsx, sort the items by cost, highest first.

source.feature: The spreadsheet editor's sort and column width operations, added to codenine_spreadsheet_edit with the editors change. Written with the operations, not from a seen failure; no paid run has graded it yet.

notes: Any row of the table is a correct anchor, so the case checks the column and the direction only. The workbook is a binary placeholder, so the case grades the route taken.

pattern: say a column cannot be resized, or script it, instead of the width operation
experience: Asked to widen a column, an agent says the spreadsheet tool cannot change widths, or opens the workbook with a library to set one. The setColumnWidth operation saves the width with the file.
rule: sort a table's rows by a column (sortRows takes any cell of the table in the column to sort by; headings and a row of totals stay where they are), set column widths
prompt: In budget.xlsx the Item column is too narrow for the names. Make it about twice as wide.

source.feature: The spreadsheet editor's sort and column width operations, added to codenine_spreadsheet_edit with the editors change. Written with the operations, not from a seen failure; no paid run has graded it yet.

notes: The width chosen is not graded, only that the width operation names the Item column.

pattern: ordinary data work that does not change an office document
experience: A user asks for a quick count over a plain-text log. This is ordinary shell work: the document tools have nothing to do with it, and a fix that makes agents avoid the shell near any tabular file overcorrects.
